items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I'm sorry that I didn't accept it in those days. I possibly would have gone a lot further than I did.

ctx.x: Yeah, you would deal with one man?

One man. How much territory? The man that first picked me up was Bernard Galway. And I had him, not only was his name, but Rabinowitz. And then finally this Al Travis that was the biggest crook in the world. And then the next biggest crook was this one that I picked up here, Chauncey Highland, on the revision of my band. Those were crooks. They weren't under bondage like the big companies are now. And the only major company that I went with that was under bonds was when I went to Joe Glazer. See, Glazer wanted me…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: That's where Ella and all these other upcoming stars. We had a big production.

ctx.x: Well, I guess sometimes you'd get top billing and sometimes you wouldn't. Well, yeah. It was very.

Top billing and most of the time in the cities but on the stages might have been a review. So, you're just another part of the review. So, for instance, this is Ralph Cooper's review. Mm-hmm. Featuring Don Albert's Big Bang. Who was Ralph Cooper? Ralph Cooper was a producer in New York. Mm-hmm. He was just like Larry Steele and those guys who don't know anything about him. I only heard their name. But they were producers. He produced the show at the Fowlers in Brooklyn. That's where Ella and all these other…
Yeah, well, that's more honest than the way they do things now sometimes. I don't know.
